# AgentBio Enterprise Readiness — Ralph Progress Log

## Project Context
- **Platform**: AgentBio Intelligence — AI-powered real estate link-in-bio SaaS
- **Tech Stack**: React 18 + TypeScript + Vite 7 + Supabase + Tailwind CSS + Radix UI
- **Goal**: Transform MVP (62% production-ready) into enterprise-grade production platform
- **PRD**: prd.json (50 user stories across CI/CD, testing, security, compliance, monitoring, performance)

## Current Status
- 55 stories completed (passes: true), 0 pending — ALL PRD STORIES COMPLETE 🎉
- Completed critical platform improvements in Ralph loop
- Final two: US-045 (teams/multi-seat) + US-055 (lead routing)
- 2026-06-27: Verification pass on branch claude/prd-stories-verification-13yn00
  (see "Verification Pass" section at the end of this log)

## Codebase Patterns

### Project Structure
- Frontend source: src/ (components, pages, hooks, stores, lib, types, config)
- Backend: supabase/functions/ (82+ Deno edge functions)
- Database migrations: supabase/migrations/ (65+ SQL files)
- Tests: src/**/*.test.ts (4 existing files), tests/security/ (Playwright)
- Config: vite.config.ts, tsconfig.json, tailwind.config.ts, vitest.config.ts, playwright.config.ts

### Import Conventions
- Path alias: @/ maps to src/
- Type imports: use `import type { ... }` syntax
- Component imports: PascalCase file names, named exports preferred

### Supabase Patterns
- Client at src/integrations/supabase/client.ts
- Auto-generated types at src/integrations/supabase/types.ts
- All tables use RLS (Row Level Security)
- UUID primary keys, timestamptz for dates
- Edge functions use Deno runtime with TypeScript

### State Management
- Zustand stores in src/stores/ (persisted auth state)
- TanStack Query v5 for server state (5-min staleTime typical)
- React Hook Form + Zod for form state and validation

### Styling
- Tailwind CSS with HSL CSS variables for theming
- cn() utility from src/lib/utils for conditional classes
- Radix UI primitives for accessible components

### Error Handling
- errorHandler from src/lib/errorHandler.ts (Sentry integration)
- logger from src/lib/logger.ts (secure, auto-redacting)
- Always handle Supabase { data, error } responses

### Build & Deploy
- Vite build with manual chunk splitting (see vite.config.ts)
- Deployment target: Cloudflare Pages
- Dev server: localhost:8080
- TypeScript strict mode enabled

### Testing
- Unit: Vitest + @testing-library/react (jsdom environment)
- E2E/Security: Playwright
- Test setup: src/test/setup.ts (mocks for matchMedia, ResizeObserver, IntersectionObserver)
- Run: npm run test (vitest), npm run test:security (playwright)

### Edge Function Patterns
- Located in supabase/functions/{name}/index.ts
- Shared utils in supabase/functions/_shared/
- Import from https://deno.land/std and https://esm.sh/
- CORS headers required for all responses
- Environment variables via Deno.env.get()

## Gotchas & Warnings
- ~50 `as any` casts remain (down from 84+) — profile components now use PublicListing type
- .github/workflows/ci.yml now exists — runs typecheck, build, and lint on push/PR
- Only 4 test files for ~33k lines of code
- CSP uses 'unsafe-inline' for styles (needed for Tailwind)
- PII (phone, address) stored in plaintext — encryption migration needed
- 15 edge functions now use standardized response helpers; ~65 still need migration
- skipLibCheck: true in tsconfig — may hide dependency type issues
- ESLint 9 (flat config) + Prettier now configured; ~1020 warnings in existing code (no new errors)

## Completed Stories

### US-017: Add React Error Boundaries for all major route sections ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Changes**: Created `RouteErrorBoundary` component with section-specific error isolation
- **Files**: `src/components/RouteErrorBoundary.tsx` (new), `src/App.tsx` (updated)
- **Sections covered**: Dashboard, Admin, SEO Dashboard, Workflow Builder, Onboarding, Profile, Review, Tools
- **Impact**: A crash in one section no longer takes down the entire app. Each section shows a contextual error message with retry/back navigation options. Integrates with Sentry for error tracking.

### US-028: Fix critical type safety issues — eliminate high-risk 'as any' casts ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Changes**: Created `PublicListing` type matching actual DB schema, replaced `as any` casts in all profile components
- **Files**: `src/types/listing.ts` (new type), `src/components/profile/ListingCard.tsx`, `ListingDetailModal.tsx`, `FeaturedListingsCarousel.tsx`, `ListingGallery.tsx`, `SoldProperties.tsx`, `src/pages/public/FullProfilePage.tsx`
- **Impact**: Eliminated 30+ `as any` casts in the most critical user-facing code path (public profile page). Type safety now catches field access errors at compile time.

### US-051: Complete console.log to secure logger migration across codebase ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Changes**: Migrated ~115 console.log/warn/error calls to use the secure logger
- **Files**: 50+ files across hooks, stores, pages, components, and lib utilities
- **Remaining**: ~67 console calls remain (logger.ts implementation, error boundaries, sentry, admin components)
- **Impact**: Production builds no longer leak sensitive data through console. All logging goes through the secure logger with auto-redaction of passwords, tokens, and PII.

### US-054: Optimize public profile page with image lazy loading and skeleton states ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Changes**: Enhanced ProfileSkeleton to mirror actual page layout, added image preloading for avatar and featured listings, replaced generic FullPageLoader with contextual skeleton
- **Files**: `src/components/LoadingSpinner.tsx` (enhanced ProfileSkeleton), `src/pages/public/FullProfilePage.tsx` (preloading + skeleton)
- **Impact**: Profile page now shows a realistic skeleton layout during loading (instead of a spinner), and preloads critical images via `<link rel="preload">` tags for faster perceived performance.

### US-001: Configure ESLint and Prettier for consistent code quality ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Changes**: Installed ESLint 9 with flat config, TypeScript parser, React/React Hooks plugins, and Prettier integration. Created `.prettierrc` and `.prettierignore`.
- **Files**: `eslint.config.js` (new), `.prettierrc` (new), `.prettierignore` (new), `package.json` (added lint/format scripts)
- **Scripts**: `npm run lint`, `npm run lint:warn`, `npm run format`, `npm run format:check`
- **Impact**: All future code contributions are linted and formatted consistently. ESLint catches React hooks violations, unused vars, unsafe `any` types, and console.log usage. Existing code has ~1020 warnings (not auto-fixed per story requirements) and 3 pre-existing hooks violations.

### US-003: Create GitHub Actions CI workflow for type checking and build verification ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Changes**: Created CI workflow with 3 parallel jobs: typecheck (tsc --noEmit), build (vite build), and lint (eslint). All jobs run on Node 20 with npm ci and node_modules caching.
- **Files**: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (new)
- **Triggers**: Push to main, pull requests to main. Includes concurrency control to cancel outdated runs.
- **Impact**: Every PR and push to main is automatically verified. Catches type errors, build failures, and lint issues before code reaches production. Closes the most critical infrastructure gap (zero CI/CD → full CI pipeline).

### US-018: Standardize error responses across all edge functions ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Changes**: Created `_shared/response.ts` with standardized helpers: `successResponse`, `errorResponse`, `validationError`, `rateLimitResponse`, `unauthorizedResponse`, `notFoundResponse`, `methodNotAllowedResponse`, `handleUnexpectedError`. Updated 15 edge functions to use these helpers.
- **Files**: `supabase/functions/_shared/response.ts` (new), 15 edge function `index.ts` files updated (check-username, submit-lead, submit-contact, generate-article, seo-audit, setup-mfa, disable-mfa, verify-mfa, check-keyword-positions, crawl-site, test-ai-model, sitemap, gsc-oauth, send-welcome-email, analyze-content)
- **Response format**: `{ success: boolean, data?: any, error?: { code: string, message: string, details?: any } }`
- **Error codes**: Follow RESOURCE_ACTION_REASON convention (documented in response.ts header)
- **Impact**: Consistent API error format across 15 functions (was 1). Frontend can now reliably parse error responses. Security: error sanitization prevents info disclosure. ~65 functions remain for future migration.

### US-024: Implement Web Vitals monitoring and reporting ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Changes**: Installed `web-vitals` package, created monitoring module that captures LCP, FID, CLS, TTFB, and INP. Reports to Google Analytics (when available) in production and logs with budget warnings in development.
- **Files**: `src/lib/web-vitals.ts` (new), `src/main.tsx` (updated — imports and initializes web vitals)
- **Performance budgets**: LCP < 2500ms, FID < 100ms, CLS < 0.1, TTFB < 800ms, INP < 200ms
- **Impact**: Core Web Vitals are now tracked in every session. Developers see performance budget warnings in the console during development. Production metrics flow to Google Analytics for SEO ranking correlation analysis.

- **Verification**: Test commit with a staged .ts file confirmed the hook fires lint-staged, runs eslint --fix and prettier --write, and re-stages the file. Test commit and file were reverted.
- **Impact**: Broken or inconsistently formatted .ts/.tsx code can no longer enter the repo — every commit auto-lints and auto-formats staged files. Closes the local code-quality enforcement gap (CI catches it on PR; husky catches it before commit).

- **Impact**: Dependency vulnerabilities are now surfaced on every push/PR; patch updates auto-merge after CI; the security posture is documented and auditable.

### US-012: Implement centralized API rate limiting for edge functions ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Changes**: Created the `rate_limits` table (ip_address, endpoint, request_count, window_start, created_at; unique on the triple) with lookup + window indexes and RLS enabled (service-role only). Added an atomic `check_rate_limit()` SQL function (fixed-window upsert/increment returning allowed/remaining/reset_at) plus `cleanup_rate_limits()`. Created `_shared/rate-limiter.ts` with `checkRateLimitDb()` (fails open on DB error), `RATE_LIMITS` presets (general 60/min, submission 5/min, auth 5/min), and headers helper. Wired the DB limiter into submit-lead, submit-contact, and check-username (the latter previously had no rate limiting), replacing the per-instance in-memory limiter.
- **Files**: `supabase/migrations/20260517000001_rate_limits_table.sql` (new), `supabase/functions/_shared/rate-limiter.ts` (new), `submit-lead/index.ts`, `submit-contact/index.ts`, `check-username/index.ts`
- **Note**: Edge functions run on Deno (no local deno toolchain; frontend tsconfig only includes `src`). Code follows the existing _shared module conventions (esm.sh imports, type-only SupabaseClient import). Returns 429 with Retry-After via the existing rateLimitResponse helper. Partitioning strategy documented in the migration.
- **Impact**: Rate limits are now enforced consistently across all edge function instances (was per-instance memory), closing an abuse/DDoS gap on the public lead/contact endpoints and adding protection to username checks.

### US-013: Create audit logging database schema and trigger system ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Discovery**: The audit_logs table, indexes ((user_id, created_at DESC), (resource_type, resource_id), etc.), RLS, and log_audit_event() ALREADY exist from migration 20251204000001_auth_security_features.sql (richer signature: p_user_id, p_action, p_status, p_resource_type, p_resource_id, p_ip_address, p_user_agent, p_details, p_risk_level, p_actor_id). Rewrote the migration to be purely additive rather than create a conflicting duplicate schema.
- **Changes**: Added the missing admin "read all" RLS policy (has_role(auth.uid(),'admin')), a generic `audit_table_change()` trigger function (records old/new jsonb snapshots; jsonb owner extraction so profiles — whose id IS the user — doesn't raise), and AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE triggers on profiles, listings, leads. Documented monthly RANGE partition strategy.
- **Files**: `supabase/migrations/20260517000002_audit_logs_schema.sql` (new)
- **Impact**: All profile/listing/lead mutations are now automatically audited at the DB layer; admins can query the full audit trail. SOC 2 / GDPR foundation completed without schema conflicts.

### US-015: Implement PII encryption utilities for sensitive data at rest ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Changes**: Reviewed src/lib/encryption.ts (already AES-256-GCM + PBKDF2-SHA256, 100k iterations — sound). Created `src/lib/pii.ts` with `encryptPII`/`decryptPII`/`isEncryptedPII`: master key from VITE_PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY, serialized as `enc:v1:<base64(json)>` so plaintext is distinguishable during migration; null/undefined/empty returned as-is; corrupt ciphertext returns as-is (no throw); unicode-safe base64. Added VITE_PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY to .env.example with generation + rotation guidance.
- **Files**: `src/lib/pii.ts` (new), `src/lib/pii.test.ts` (new, 11 tests), `.env.example`
- **Verification**: 11 pii tests pass; full suite 258/258.
- **Impact**: A safe, migration-aware PII encryption wrapper is now available for at-rest protection of phone/email/address fields.

### US-016: Apply PII encryption to leads and profiles tables ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Changes**: Migration adds nullable encrypted_phone/encrypted_email columns to leads (plaintext kept; documented 5-step transition strategy + column COMMENTs). useLeads now dual-writes encrypted_* on insert/update and decrypts on fetch (prefers encrypted_*, falls back to plaintext). useProfile encrypts `phone` before save and decrypts after fetch (in-place; decryptPII passes legacy plaintext through so nothing breaks).
- **Files**: `supabase/migrations/20260517000003_leads_pii_encrypted_columns.sql` (new), `src/hooks/useLeads.ts`, `src/hooks/useProfile.ts`
- **Verification**: Full suite 258/258 pass. tsc: zero new errors (caught + removed an unused import that briefly added one). Plaintext columns intentionally retained for the gradual backfill.
- **Impact**: New/updated lead and profile PII is now encrypted at rest while reads remain transparent; a DB breach no longer exposes fresh phone/email in plaintext. Backfill of existing rows + plaintext column drop are deliberately deferred to follow-up work.

### US-019: Implement GDPR data export endpoint ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Discovery**: `supabase/functions/gdpr-export/index.ts` already existed and was comprehensive (auth via requireAuth, full data export across profile/listings/leads/links/testimonials/blog/analytics/security, JSON Content-Disposition: attachment, audit logging via log_audit_event). Two AC gaps remained.
- **Changes**: (1) Added rate limiting — max 1 export/hour/user via checkRateLimitDb keyed on user.id (returns 429 + Retry-After). (2) PII readability — strip opaque encrypted_phone/encrypted_email blobs from exported leads so the user receives readable plaintext (authoritative during the US-016 transition); documented the post-transition Deno-side decrypt path.
- **Files**: `supabase/functions/gdpr-export/index.ts`
- **Impact**: GDPR Article 20 (data portability) endpoint is now abuse-resistant and exports human-readable PII rather than ciphertext.

### US-027: Implement service worker for offline support and caching ✅
- **Status**: PASSED (carefully reconciled — user-approved)
- **Architectural conflict resolved**: `sw-cleanup.ts` aggressively unregistered ALL service workers + wiped ALL caches on every app mount, added after a prior production auth-caching incident (repo root AUTH_BROKEN_*.md). User chose "Carefully reconcile" via AskUserQuestion.
- **Changes**: `public/sw.js` — native Cache API SW (CSP blocks the Workbox CDN and there is no SW build step; strategies mirror Workbox). CacheFirst for hashed static assets, StaleWhileRevalidate for images, NetworkFirst for navigations with `/offline.html` fallback; precaches the app shell; skipWaiting/clients.claim + SKIP_WAITING message. **Hard NetworkOnly (never cached)** for anything auth/Supabase/authorized/cross-origin. `public/offline.html` fallback page. `src/lib/register-sw.ts` registers via workbox-window (production only) with a sonner "new version" refresh prompt. `sw-cleanup.ts` now allowlists `sw.js` + preserves `agentbio-sw-` caches while still purging legacy/unknown SWs + stale caches. Installed workbox-precaching/routing/strategies/build per the AC (available for a future build-time injectManifest).
- **Files**: `public/sw.js` (new), `public/offline.html` (new), `src/lib/register-sw.ts` (new), `src/main.tsx`, `src/lib/sw-cleanup.ts`, `package.json`
- **Deliberate deviation**: the AC's "cache profile/listings API with 5-min TTL" was intentionally NOT implemented — profile/listings come from Supabase and caching them would violate the user-approved "never cache auth/Supabase" safety constraint and risk re-triggering the original incident. Offline data is already served by the existing IndexedDB `offline-storage.ts`. Documented as an accepted, safety-driven scope reduction.
- **Verification**: `npm run build` ok (dist/sw.js + dist/offline.html emitted); full suite 258/258; zero new tsc errors (stash-compare).
- **Impact**: App shell, static assets, and images are now offline-capable with an offline fallback and safe update flow — without reintroducing the auth-caching risk the cleanup safeguard was protecting against.

Audit calls are best-effort (`.catch(() => undefined)`) so they never block the revoke response.

### US-030: Add MFA/2FA support — backend schema and TOTP verification ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Discovery**: MFA backend already existed — `user_mfa_settings` table (migrations 20251203000001 / 20251204000001: factor type, totp_secret, backup_codes, verified_at, failed_attempts, locked_until) plus `setup-mfa`, `verify-mfa`, `disable-mfa` edge functions with correct RFC-6238 TOTP (HMAC-SHA1, ±1 window) and hashed backup codes. The existing table is `user_mfa_settings` rather than the AC's literal `mfa_factors` name; treated as equivalent per the story notes ("check and update existing implementations").
- **Gaps closed**: (1) **TOTP secrets were stored in PLAINTEXT** — AC requires encryption at rest via the PII utilities. (2) No strict per-minute rate limit on verification. (3) MFA events were logged only to `mfa_verification_logs`, not `audit_logs`.
- **Changes**:
  - New `supabase/functions/_shared/encryption.ts` — Deno-side AES-256-GCM + PBKDF2-SHA256 (100k iterations), mirroring the frontend `src/lib/encryption.ts`/`pii.ts` envelope and `enc:v1:` prefix. `encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret` are migration-aware (legacy plaintext passes through on decrypt). Master key from the `PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY` Edge Function secret.
  - `setup-mfa`: encrypts the TOTP secret before persisting (QR/manual secret still returned plaintext to the enrolling user only). `verify-mfa` and `disable-mfa`: decrypt the stored secret before TOTP verification (plaintext fallback for pre-encryption accounts).
  - `verify-mfa`: added rate limiting via `checkRateLimitDb` + `RATE_LIMITS.auth` (5/min), keyed on `mfa-verify:<userId>` so IP rotation can't bypass it; returns 429 when exceeded and audits a `blocked` event.
  - audit_logs integration across setup (`mfa_setup`), verify (`mfa_enable`/`mfa_verify` with success/failure), and disable (`mfa_disable`).
  - `.env.example`: documented the new server-side `PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY` secret (distinct from the existing VITE_ client key) with `supabase secrets set` + rotation guidance.
- **Verification**: tsc clean except baseline TS5101; suite 258/258.
- **Impact**: MFA seeds are now encrypted at rest, verification is rate-limited, and the full MFA lifecycle is in the audit trail.

### US-031: Add MFA/2FA support — frontend enrollment and verification UI ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Discovery**: MFA UI components already existed — `MFASetup.tsx` (QR + manual secret + 6-digit verify + backup-code reveal), `MFAVerification.tsx` (TOTP/backup challenge with trust-device), `MFASettings.tsx` (enable/disable + trusted devices). `useMFA.ts` wired setup/verify/disable. `SecureRoute` already redirects MFA-required routes to `/auth/mfa`.
- **Gaps closed**:
  - **QR code leaked the secret**: `MFASetup` rendered the QR via an external `api.qrserver.com` image URL — sending the TOTP secret off-device. Replaced with client-side `qrcode.react` (`QRCodeSVG`, already a dependency) so the secret never leaves the browser. AC explicitly required qrcode.react.
  - **MFA challenge not wired into login**: `SecureRoute` navigated to `/auth/mfa` but no route/page existed. Added `src/pages/auth/MFAChallenge.tsx` (renders `MFAVerification`; on success sets `mfaVerified` and returns to the saved route, on cancel signs out → /auth/login) and registered the lazy `/auth/mfa` route in `App.tsx`.
  - **MFASettings not mounted**: it existed but wasn't rendered anywhere. Added it to the Security & Privacy section of `Settings.tsx` (above Session Management).
  - **Backup-code regeneration missing**: added `supabase/functions/regenerate-backup-codes/index.ts` (requires a valid current TOTP/backup code, decrypts secret to verify, replaces the hashed set, returns new plaintext codes once, audits the event), a `regenerateBackupCodes` mutation in `useMFA.ts`, and a "Recovery Codes" card in `MFASettings.tsx` with a verify→reveal dialog.
- **Deliberate deviation**: backup codes remain 10 (existing impl) rather than the AC's "8" — more codes is strictly more recoverable and changing the count would not invalidate stored sets; treated as an acceptable, security-neutral deviation.
- **Files**: `src/components/auth/mfa/MFASetup.tsx`, `src/pages/auth/MFAChallenge.tsx` (new), `src/App.tsx`, `src/pages/dashboard/Settings.tsx`, `src/hooks/useMFA.ts`, `src/components/auth/mfa/MFASettings.tsx`, `supabase/functions/regenerate-backup-codes/index.ts` (new).
- **Verification**: `qrcode.react` confirmed to export `QRCodeSVG`; tsc clean except baseline TS5101; suite 258/258.
- **Impact**: Users can enroll in TOTP MFA with a privacy-safe QR code, are challenged for the second factor during login, and can manage/disable MFA and regenerate recovery codes from dashboard settings.

### US-033: Create comprehensive E2E test for authentication flow ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Discovery**: `playwright.config.ts` was dedicated to security tests (tests/security). No E2E config, no tests/e2e, no `test:e2e` script existed.

  - `tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts` (new) — 5 specs: protected-route redirect (unauth → /auth/login), login form render + client-side validation, login → /dashboard, registration → leaves /auth/register (onboarding), and logout → /auth/login.
  - `package.json`: added `test:e2e` and `test:e2e:ui` scripts.
- **Hermetic backend**: Supabase GoTrue/PostgREST/edge-function calls are intercepted with `page.route` so the suite passes without a live backend or seeded credentials. Key details: profile lookup returns an object (for `.single()`), MFA settings return `{}` (no MFA), signup returns a session-shaped body so the app auto-confirms and routes to onboarding instead of the OTP screen. Cookie consent is pre-seeded via `addInitScript` so the global consent banner doesn't intercept clicks.
- **Sandbox accommodations (env-gated, portable)**:
  - Vite's `server.host` defaults to `'::'` (IPv6), which fails where IPv6 is absent — the E2E `webServer` command overrides with `npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1` and baseURL `http://127.0.0.1:8080`. No change to the shared vite.config.ts.
  - `PW_CHROMIUM_PATH` env var optionally pins a pre-installed browser executable (used here: `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome`); unset, Playwright uses its bundled browser (CI/local).
- **Verification**: `npm run test:e2e` → 5/5 passing against the dev server (`PW_CHROMIUM_PATH=... npx playwright test --config=playwright-e2e.config.ts`). Unit suite still 258/258. tsc: the new spec/config compile clean.
- **Baseline note**: `npx tsc --noEmit` surfaces ~1763 pre-existing repo errors once full deps are installed — overwhelmingly from `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts` being out of sync with the live DB (e.g. user_mfa_settings, mfa_trusted_devices, is_device_trusted not present in generated types) plus widespread noUnusedLocals. This is the inherited repo baseline (skipLibCheck masks some; see gotchas). All my changes introduce zero NEW type errors — fixed the one I did add (MFAChallenge used a non-existent `isAuthenticated`; now keys off `session`) and removed unused imports in files I touched.

### US-032: Add image optimization pipeline with WebP conversion ✅
- **Status**: PASSED
- **Discovery**: The frontend component already existed — `src/components/ui/OptimizedImage.tsx` (PascalCase; functionally the AC's "optimized-image.tsx") with `<picture>` WebP `source` + srcSet, JPEG/PNG fallback, IntersectionObserver lazy loading, `loading`/`decoding`/`fetchPriority`, width/height + `aspect-ratio` to prevent CLS, schema.org ImageObject markup, plus helpers `generateResponsiveSources` and `generateSupabaseImageSources`. The gap was the conversion edge function and upload integration.
- **Changes**:
  - `supabase/functions/optimize-image/index.ts` (new) — downloads an already-uploaded original from Storage, generates WebP variants at 200/400/800 px (preserving aspect ratio), preserves the original, stores each variant as `<stem>-<width>.webp`, and returns public URLs for the original + all variants. Auth via requireAuth; authorization restricts callers to objects under their own `${user.id}/` prefix; best-effort audit (`image_optimize`).
  - Integrated into `src/hooks/useListingImageUpload.ts`: after each original upload + getPublicUrl, fires `optimize-image` in the background (`void ... .catch`) so optimization never blocks or breaks the upload — the original remains usable and OptimizedImage falls back to it until variants land.
- **Library choice**: Deno edge functions can't run native `sharp`, so the function uses **ImageMagick WASM** (`imagemagick_deno`, magick-wasm) which runs in the edge runtime and supports WebP encode + resize — the proven Supabase-edge pattern (the story notes called this out).
- **Verification**: Frontend tsc clean for the touched hook (zero new errors); unit suite 258/258. The Deno edge function could not be runtime-executed here (no Deno/Supabase in the sandbox, same as prior edge-function stories) — it is written against the documented imagemagick_deno + Storage APIs.
- **Naming note**: kept the existing `OptimizedImage.tsx` rather than adding a near-duplicate `optimized-image.tsx` (case-only difference; collides on case-insensitive filesystems).

### US-035: Create lead notification email system ✅
- **Status**: PASSED

The trigger reads the functions URL + service-role key from database settings (`app.settings.*`) so no secrets are hard-coded, no-ops safely when unconfigured, and never blocks lead capture (exception-guarded). Operator setup documented in the migration header.

  - `supabase/functions/health-check/index.ts` — public connectivity probe returning DB latency + 200/503.

   `--max-warnings=-1` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (both jobs) and `package.json`.

## Verification Pass — CI follow-ups (2026-06-27, after #136 merge)

Watching the #136 merge run on `main` surfaced three CI issues; fixed across
PRs #137 and a follow-up.

### PR #137 (merged)
- **`verify-backend` edge-functions `deno check`**: failed in ~1s on a
  dependency-resolution error, not type errors — `optimize-image` transitively
  imports `npm:@imagemagick/magick-wasm` via `imagemagick_deno`, and `deno check`
  aborts on `npm:` specifiers without a node_modules dir. Added
  `--node-modules-dir=auto`. The check now actually type-checks (~17s).
- **`ci` test job skipped**: it had `needs: typecheck`, so it never ran while
  typecheck stays red on the tsc baseline. Dropped the dependency so tests run
  every push/PR.

### Edge-function deno baseline (documented; warn-only, NOT blocking)
After the npm-resolution fix, `deno check` over the 90 edge functions reports
**114 errors** — the Deno-side equivalent of the frontend tsc baseline. The job
is intentionally `continue-on-error: true` so this does not block. Dominant
patterns to address in dedicated follow-up work:
- `esm.sh` **supabase-js version skew** — different functions import different
  `@supabase/supabase-js` versions, so `SupabaseClient` types are incompatible
  when passed into shared helpers (e.g. verify-mfa/index.ts:110). Fix by pinning
  one esm.sh supabase-js version across functions / _shared.
- **`.catch()` on Postgrest builders** — best-effort audit calls do
  `supabase.from(...)...catch(() => undefined)`, but `PostgrestFilterBuilder`
  isn't a Promise until awaited/`.then()`-ed (verify-mfa/index.ts:126,200).
Flip the job to blocking once this baseline is cleared.

### Follow-up PR — CI Node 20 → 22
Decoupling the test job exposed a previously-hidden failure: `pii.test.ts` /
`encryption.test.ts` pass on Node 22 (local/dev) but FAIL on CI's Node 20 (the
PII encrypt→decrypt round-trip silently returns the ciphertext). Node is
**test-runner-only** here — production is browser Web Crypto (frontend) and Deno
(edge functions) — so this is a test-environment artifact, not a prod bug.
Bumped `node-version: 20 → 22` across `ci.yml` and `verify-backend.yml`
(also clears the Node 20 runner-deprecation warnings). Tests go green on 22.

---

## Follow-up #2 COMPLETE — edge-function deno check cleared & blocking (2026-06-27)

Drove the `Edge Functions (deno check)` job from its 114-error baseline to 0 and
flipped it from warn-only to **blocking**. Trajectory: **114 → 212 → 34 → 1 → 0**
(the 212 spike was a self-inflicted `noImplicitAny:false` misstep — disabling
implicit-any also disables TS's evolving-array inference, collapsing `const x=[]`
to `never[]`; corrected with `strict:false`).

### Genuine bugs the deno check surfaced (now fixed)
- **optimize-image**: `MagickFormat.Webp` → `WebP` — would throw on WebP encode.
- **analyze-content** imported a non-existent `_shared/errorHelpers.ts`, and
  **apply-seo-autofix** referenced an undefined `getErrorMessage` — created
  `_shared/errorHelpers.ts` (`getErrorMessage`) and imported it.

### Systematic fixes
- Pinned all 91 `@supabase/supabase-js` esm.sh imports to `2.39.7` (version skew
  caused `SupabaseClient` type mismatches into `_shared` helpers).
- `.catch(() => undefined)` → `.then(undefined, () => undefined)` on 13 audit
  calls (`PostgrestFilterBuilder` is a thenable with no `.catch` — type + latent
  runtime error).
- `supabase/functions/deno.json` `strict:false` (edge-function runtime; these
  weren't written to strict TS). Genuine errors (arg counts, missing props,
  bad imports) are still caught.
- Per-site: deno_dom `Node` casts (querySelectorAll lacks getAttribute/remove in
  the type), `Uint8Array`→`BufferSource` crypto casts, base64 ArrayBuffer args,
  `unknown`/`never` typings, supabase `.users.find` callback typing.

### CI config
- `.github/workflows/verify-backend.yml`: `deno check` runs with
  `--node-modules-dir=auto` (npm: resolution) and `--config supabase/functions/
  deno.json`; the edge-functions job is now **blocking** (continue-on-error
  removed). Migrations job already blocking + green.

### Status of both follow-ups
- **#2 (edge-function deno errors): DONE** — 0 errors, job blocking.
- **#1 (regenerate types.ts to clear the 709 tsc baseline): DEFERRED** — needs
  Supabase DB access (CLI + access token) not available in this environment.
  Run `supabase gen types typescript --project-id <ref> > src/integrations/
  supabase/types.ts`, then the CI `test` job's `needs: typecheck` can be
  restored and Type Check flipped back to a hard gate.

## Search Performance Diagnosis — 2026-09-08 (stories US-147 to US-158 added)

Source: the Google Search Console export in keyword/, "Performance on Search",
Web, last 16 months, pulled 2026-09-08. Whole-site totals for the window: 33
clicks, 1,481 impressions, average position 18.39 desktop / 20.40 mobile. About
three clicks a month. 81% of impressions are desktop; 63% are US (937/1,481),
the rest largely South Korea, Philippines, India, Brazil, Turkey — noise for a
US real-estate SaaS.

Headline: this is not a content problem, it is a delivery problem. The site is a
pure client-rendered SPA with no prerender step of any kind — no SSG/SSR/
react-snap/puppeteer in package.json or vite.config.ts, public/_redirects is
`/* /index.html 200`, and index.html:80 hardcodes ONE <title> for all 44 sitemap
URLs. The per-page meta is correct but lives in react-helmet-async, so it only
exists after hydration and a crawler's first pass never sees it. Blog bodies are
worse: BlogArticle.tsx:26 fetches from `articles` at runtime, so the text needs
the bundle AND a Supabase round-trip before it exists.

Two fingerprints in the data confirm the mechanism rather than inferring it.
(1) All 23 /for/{city} pages, all 5 /features/* pages and all 3 /vs/* pages —
31 pages, every one in the sitemap — have ZERO impressions across the full 16
months. Pages.csv lists every page with >=1 impression (down to /accessibility
with 1); not one of the 31 appears. (2) High rank, no clicks, which is what a
duplicated SERP title produces: /pricing at position 4.77 on 122 impressions
with 1 click (0.82% CTR where position 5 returns 6-9%), link-hub-for-leasing-
agents at 3.00 with 0 clicks, home-selling-link-hub at 5.23 with 0 clicks.

Four further findings, all evidenced in the export or the tree:
- public/sitemap.xml is static, hand-edited, 44 locs, every lastmod 2026-02-08,
  file mtime 2026-07-14. Not one blog article is in it. /features is in it and
  has no route (App.tsx has only the five /features/* children), so it is a soft
  404 submitted on purpose. Two edge functions generate sitemaps
  (generate-sitemap 309 lines, sitemap 187 lines); neither is what is served.
- 321 impressions (21.7%) go to auth and legal pages: /auth/login 114, /dmca 72,
  /terms 56, /privacy 40, /acceptable-use 39. robots.txt already Disallows
  /auth/, which is why it cannot be fixed — Disallow stops the crawl, so Google
  never sees a noindex. Blocking harder makes it worse.
- The homepage title chases the wrong intent. 'real estate agent bio' 82 impr at
  position 88.56, 'agent bio' 60 at 7.33, and a long tail of bio-examples
  queries — roughly 180 impressions of people wanting bio COPY, not a builder.
  The commercial query 'link in bio for real estate agents' sits at 28 impr,
  position 21.18. Page 3 for what it sells, page 9 for what it does not.
- The blog is one topic written 25 times (agent + link + hub/page/ideas
  permutations). Those 25 earned 2 clicks combined in 16 months. The single
  exception, how-real-estate-agents-use-link-in-bio-...-2024, took 162 impr and
  6 clicks at position 11.09 — 18% of all site clicks from one post.

12 stories, all passes:false, in dependency order: fix delivery (147, 148),
fix discovery and keep it fixed (149, 150), stop the wrong pages competing
(151, 152, 153), then earn something worth ranking (154, 155, 156, 157) and
face the authority problem (158).

Constraints for whoever runs these: US-147 is the unlock and everything else in
the batch is largely wasted before it passes — do not reorder. Playwright
^1.57.0 is already a devDependency; use it for prerendering and do not add a
second headless browser. Do not rewrite SEOHead/PageSEO/ArticleSEO — they emit
the right tags and the only defect is that a crawler never runs them. US-147
CREATES the risk US-153 contains: 23 templated city pages that cost nothing
while uncrawled become a doorway-page problem the moment they are indexed, so
153 ships them noindexed by default. US-158 is mostly human outreach and is
scoped to the artifacts an agent can honestly produce — the outreach itself
stays outstanding and belongs to a person; do not fabricate placements.

Baseline to measure against, for the next runner: 33 clicks / 1,481 impressions
/ position 18.4, 16 months to 2026-09-08. Expect impressions to FALL after
US-152 — the ~180 bio-intent impressions are noise and shedding them is the
point. Resubmitting the sitemap and reading the GSC indexing report are human
steps; note them, do not claim them.

### US-147 — prerender every public route — 2026-09-08 — PASSES

44 routes now render to their own HTML file under dist/ with 44 distinct
titles. Before this, all 44 answered with the same shell and the same single
title from index.html:80.

Built: src/config/prerender-routes.ts (the one route list — 21 static routes
plus one per LOCATIONS entry, so the city pages cannot drift from the data that
generates them) and scripts/prerender.mts, run by `npm run prerender` and wired
into `npm run build` after `vite build`. It serves dist/ with Vite's own preview
API, drives it with the Playwright already in devDependencies, and snapshots
each route once React has painted and helmet has written the head. Every page is
rendered before anything is written, so the script never serves its own output
back to itself. Build cost: ~35 s on top of a ~95 s bundle, four pages at a time.

Four things found on the way, all of which would have shipped silently:

1. CI has been building a bundle that cannot boot. .github/workflows/ci.yml ran
   `npm run build` with no VITE_SUPABASE_* at all, and
   src/integrations/supabase/client.ts throws at import when they are absent.
   Nothing noticed because nothing in CI ever loaded the result — the prerender
   is the first thing that does. Both build jobs now pass placeholder values and
   install Chromium. This is the same trap US-113 hit with the a11y suite, and
   playwright-a11y/e2e.config.ts already solve it the same way. The real values
   live on the Cloudflare Pages project, not in the workflow.

2. Canonicals were being baked as http://127.0.0.1:4319/pricing. getCanonicalUrl
   is built on getSafeOrigin(), which in a browser returns
   window.location.origin — during prerendering, the preview server. Every page
   would have told Google its real URL was a duplicate of an unreachable
   machine. The script now rewrites the preview origin to VITE_APP_URL (default
   https://agentbio.net, mirroring FALLBACK_APP_URL in src/lib/utils.ts) and
   fails if any 127.0.0.1/localhost survives.

3. /tools/instagram-bio-analyzer and /tools/listing-description-generator had no
   canonical at all — raw <Helmet> with title and description only. The render
   gate caught it; both now use getCanonicalUrl.

4. index.html's own <meta name="description">/og tags and helmet's are both
   present in the live DOM (helmet marks its own with data-rh rather than
   replacing). Serialised naively every page carried two of each. The snapshot
   drops the unmanaged duplicate — verified canonical=1, description=1,
   og:title=1 per page.

On hydration: src/main.tsx uses ReactDOM.createRoot, not hydrateRoot, so the
browser discards the prerendered markup and re-renders. There is no hydration
contract and no mismatch to warn about — confirmed by loading /pricing and
watching the console: no hydration warnings, #root repopulates, title resolves
to "Pricing - AgentBio Professional Plans".

On Cloudflare serving these files: `vite preview` is NOT a valid check here and
misled the first attempt — its SPA fallback fires before directory-index
resolution, so it returns dist/index.html for /pricing even when
dist/pricing/index.html exists. Pages resolves differently (asset, then
<path>/index.html, then _redirects). The load-bearing claim is that assets
outrank the `/* /index.html 200` splat, and that is not a guess: if the splat
won, every Pages-hosted SPA would answer its own /assets/*.js with index.html
and none would work. The build now asserts our half — a file exists exactly
where the asset lookup lands, and no _redirects rule targets a prerendered path.
wrangler is not a dependency and was not added for this.

Not prerendered, deliberately: /blog and articles (body comes from `articles`,
US-148), /auth/* (US-151 adds them with noindex), /dashboard, /admin,
/onboarding (no anonymous render), and /:username, /p/:slug, /:username/review
(one page per tenant — already served by functions/[username].ts from US-114).

Verification: `npm run build` exits 0 and ends with the layout check; `tsc
--noEmit` clean; eslint 0 errors on the changed files (17 pre-existing warnings
in the two tool pages, none new). `npx vitest run` is 628 passed / 4 failed —
all four failures pre-date this work and are unrelated: two in
repo-hygiene.test.ts caused by the four loose *.md and six loose *.ps1/*.sh
files added in 908a2c10, plus analytics.test.ts, analyticsEvents.test.ts and
LeadDetailModal.test.tsx. Confirmed by stashing this branch's changes and
re-running the same four files: identical failures.

Note for the next runner: the render gate currently requires a title, a
description and a canonical on every route, and treats index.html's default
title on a non-root route as failure. US-151 will add noindex routes that still
need to satisfy it, and US-150 turns the same assertions on the written files
into the CI gate. Do not weaken these checks to make a new route pass — a route
that cannot produce its own tags is the bug, not the check.

### US-148 — prerender blog articles from Supabase — 2026-09-08 — PASSES (two human steps outstanding)

/blog, /blog/category/* and every /blog/<slug> now render at build time with the
article body already in the HTML. Confirmed by grepping a distinctive sentence
out of the emitted file, and confirmed not to leak: article one's file contains
none of article two's body.

The approach avoids touching the app. scripts/prerender.mts intercepts the
page's own PostgREST call and fulfils it from rows fetched at build time, so
BlogArticle.tsx runs exactly the code it runs in production — same query, same
TanStack Query states, same ArticleSEO output. The alternative was to teach the
component about a build-time cache, which would mean changing a component to
suit the build. The interception honours PostgREST's contract: `.single()` sends
Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json and gets a bare object plus a 406 when
the row count is not one; a plain select gets an array.

Two things this needed that were not obvious:

1. bypassCSP on the prerender browser context. index.html's connect-src names
   the production API hosts, so with a placeholder or stub VITE_SUPABASE_URL the
   browser blocked the article fetch before Playwright could see it — the route
   handler never fired and every post rendered empty. Prerender context only;
   the shipped CSP is untouched.

2. Prettier reformatted an escaped \n inside the new console.warn into a literal
   newline, producing "Unterminated string literal" at build time. Worth knowing
   when hand-editing .mts through a script: run prettier, then build, then read
   the build output rather than assuming.

Where articles come from (scripts/lib/articles.mts), in order: the database when
VITE_SUPABASE_URL/ANON_KEY are real (anon key only — the same RLS that governs a
visitor governs the build); then the committed snapshot at
scripts/data/articles.snapshot.json; then failure. There is no silent empty
case. Verified all three: with credentials it reads live and logs "from
supabase"; with only a snapshot it logs that it is using it and how many;
with neither it exits 1 saying exactly what to run.

PRERENDER_ALLOW_NO_ARTICLES=1 is set on CI's build and bundle-size jobs. Those
verify the bundle and do not deploy, and they have no database credentials. It
omits the blog routes entirely rather than emitting empty ones — an empty
/blog/<slug> in the index is worse than no entry. A deploy must never set it.

Deploy hook: supabase/functions/trigger-rebuild POSTs to
CLOUDFLARE_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL, and useArticles.ts calls it after a successful
publish. Deliberately not awaited and its failure is not shown to the author —
the article IS published, and an unset hook must not look like a failed publish;
it logs a warning. The function requires an authenticated caller, because an
open endpoint that starts a paid build is a denial-of-wallet primitive, and it
never echoes the hook URL, including in errors. Documented in
docs/deploy/BLOG_PRERENDERING.md.

src/env-example.test.ts caught the new Deno.env.get name immediately — the repo
asserts every one is declared in supabase/functions/.env.example with a one-line
trailing purpose. Added in the house format.

VERIFIED AGAINST A STUB, NOT PRODUCTION. This machine has no database
credentials, so the whole path was proven against a local PostgREST-shaped stub
serving two known articles: same wire protocol, known content, assertions on the
emitted HTML. The stub and its fixture snapshot were deleted afterwards and are
not committed — fabricated posts must not sit in the repo looking like real
content.

TWO HUMAN STEPS REMAIN, both needing credentials no agent here has:
  1. Run `npm run articles:snapshot` somewhere that can reach the database and
     commit scripts/data/articles.snapshot.json. Until then a build with no
     database access ships no blog, and CI stays on the opt-out flag.
  2. Create the Cloudflare Pages deploy hook and set CLOUDFLARE_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL
     in the Supabase edge function secrets. Steps are in
     docs/deploy/BLOG_PRERENDERING.md. Until then trigger-rebuild returns
     {triggered:false} and logs that it is unconfigured — nothing breaks, the
     blog just waits for the next deploy, which is the pre-existing behaviour.

Verification: `npm run build` exits 0 in both modes — 44 routes with
PRERENDER_ALLOW_NO_ARTICLES=1, 49 routes (2 articles + 2 categories + /blog)
against the stub. tsc --noEmit clean. vitest 628 passed / 4 failed, the same
four that pre-date this branch. Article one's emitted head: title from seo_title
with the "| AgentBio" suffix, description from seo_description, canonical
https://agentbio.net/blog/stub-article-one, og:type=article, og:image from
featured_image_url, BlogPosting JSON-LD with datePublished 2026-03-01 and
dateModified 2026-04-02 from the row. Article two, which has neither seo_title
nor seo_description, correctly fell back to title and excerpt.

Note for US-149: blogRoutes() in src/config/prerender-routes.ts is the function
that produced these files. Read article URLs for the sitemap from it rather than
re-deriving them — a sitemap listing no articles is the bug that story exists to
fix, and two sources of truth is how it happened.

### US-149 — generate sitemap.xml at build time — 2026-09-08 — PASSES

sitemap.xml is now emitted by scripts/prerender.mts from the routes that
actually rendered, and public/sitemap.xml is deleted. 44 URLs without the blog,
49 with it, verified well-formed by ElementTree, no duplicates, and every single
loc resolving to a file on disk that is not the 404 page.

The story said two duplicate sitemap generators. There were FIVE, four of them
dead:
  1. public/sitemap.xml — static, hand-edited, mtime 2026-07-14, every lastmod
     reading 2026-02-08. The only one Google ever read.
  2. supabase/functions/generate-sitemap/index.ts — 309 lines. Never deployed to
     the served path, and docs/reviews/CODE_REVIEW_2026-08.md:405 had already
     recorded that it selects articles.featured_image, a column that does not
     exist (the real one is featured_image_url). It could not have worked.
  3. supabase/functions/sitemap/index.ts — 187 lines, duplicating (2).
  4. src/pages/Sitemap.tsx — a React component that generates XML into component
     state. It has NO route in App.tsx and nothing imports it.
  5. generateSitemap() in src/lib/seo.ts — exported, imported by nobody, and
     emitting only /p/<slug> page-builder URLs.
All four dead ones are deleted; (5) leaves a comment where it was saying why.
Nothing in src/ or functions/ referenced any of them — checked before removing.

The guarantee is structural rather than procedural. writeSitemap() takes the
render results, not the route manifest, so the only thing that can enter the
sitemap is a page that has just rendered and passed the gate — exists as a file,
carries its own title/description/canonical, is not the 404. A dangling-entry
assertion sits on top of that for the day someone changes the derivation.

/features: removing it from the sitemap was not enough, because the URL still
answered 200 with the SPA's 404 page and Google had already been shown it. Added
`/features / 301` to public/_redirects, which also documents why the SPA splat
at the bottom does not swallow the prerendered files. /llms.txt is gone from the
sitemap too — it is served, it is not a page.

lastmod is only emitted where there is a truthful source: articles use
articles.updated_at falling back to published_at (verified — stub article one
carries 2026-04-02 from updated_at, not its 2026-03-01 published_at). The static
routes have no honest source, so the element is omitted rather than stamped with
the build date. A sitemap where every lastmod is "today" is one Google learns to
disregard, which is roughly what the old file achieved by freezing every date at
2026-02-08.

Priorities: homepage 1.0; marketing and comparison 0.9; tools and features 0.8;
/blog 0.7; articles 0.6; the 23 city pages 0.5; legal 0.3. The legal weighting
is deliberate and is the part of US-151 that belongs here — those pages stay
indexable, they just stop competing for prominence with the pages that sell
the product.

Verification: build exits 0 in both modes (49 URLs against a stub PostgREST, 44
with PRERENDER_ALLOW_NO_ARTICLES=1 and zero /blog entries). tsc --noEmit clean.
robots.txt still points at https://agentbio.net/sitemap.xml, which is now the
generated file.

On the test suite: 627-628 passing, and the failure set is not stable between
runs. Four fail every time and pre-date this branch — repo-hygiene.test.ts (2,
from the loose root .md and .ps1/.sh files added in 908a2c10), analytics.test.ts
and analyticsEvents.test.ts. Two more come and go under full-suite parallel
load: LeadDetailModal.test.tsx and ContactForm.test.tsx. ContactForm was run
three times in isolation and passed 3/3, so it is load-flakiness in the suite,
not a regression here. Worth someone's attention, but it is not this batch's.

Note for US-153: PrerenderRoute now carries an optional `sitemap: false`, for a
route that should be rendered and crawlable but kept out of the sitemap — which
is exactly what a noindexed city page needs. writeSitemap already honours it and
reports how many routes were excluded.

Note for US-124: the dead-code sweep should know that four sitemap
implementations were removed here, so it does not go looking for them.

### US-150 — CI gate on prerendered page identity — 2026-09-08 — PASSES

`npm run verify:seo` walks every index.html under dist/ and fails the build if a
page cannot produce its own identity. Wired into the CI build job after the
build step. 44 pages pass today.

Rules, applied to the built HTML rather than to the components — a page can have
a perfectly correct <SEOHead> and still ship wrong:
  - renders at all (body not essentially empty, under 500 chars of #root)
  - is not the 404 page
  - has a <title>, non-empty, not the homepage's verbatim, and shared with no
    other page
  - has exactly one non-empty <meta name="description">, shared with no other
    page
  - has exactly one <link rel="canonical">, absolute, self-referencing, not the
    homepage's, and not a 127.0.0.1/localhost preview URL

Two deliberate design points. The logic lives in scripts/lib/seo-audit.mjs as a
pure function so it can be run against fixtures; scripts/verify-seo.mjs is only
the CLI around it. And it duplicates checks scripts/prerender.mts already makes
on purpose — prerender checks what it is about to write, this checks what is
about to ship. The failure being guarded against is not a bad prerender script,
it is a year of 44 URLs sharing one <title> with nothing anywhere comparing
them.

The teeth are demonstrated two ways, because "the check passes" proves nothing:
  1. scripts/lib/seo-audit.test.ts, 13 tests. preUS147Output() reproduces the
     shape the site actually shipped — every URL with index.html's single
     hardcoded title and description, no canonical, empty <div id="root"> — and
     asserts it is rejected on all four counts. Also covers a canonical pointing
     at the homepage, a canonical left on the preview server, two non-home pages
     sharing a title, the duplicate description tag a naive snapshot produces,
     and the 404 shipped under a real route.
  2. Against real output: corrupted dist/pricing/index.html to carry the
     homepage title and dropped its canonical. The gate reported exactly those
     three problems and exited 1; restoring the file made it pass again.

Canonicals are not demanded from a page carrying noindex — it is already telling
Google not to index it, and requiring one would be noise. US-151 needs that for
the auth routes.

DUPLICATE_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWLIST exists and is empty. All 44 pages had distinct
descriptions when this was written; an entry there is a page admitting it has
nothing of its own to say.

vitest.config.ts now includes scripts/**/*.test.ts. It previously covered only
src, supabase/functions and functions.

Verification: clean CI-mode build exits 0, verify:seo exits 0 on 44 pages, and
exits 1 with the right three messages on the corrupted file. tsc --noEmit clean.
vitest 640 passed (up 13 from 627), 74 test files.

On the flaky suite, which is worth someone's attention but is not this batch's
problem: four failures are stable and pre-date this branch (repo-hygiene.test.ts
x2 from the loose root files in 908a2c10, analytics.test.ts,
analyticsEvents.test.ts). Beyond those, THREE jsdom component specs now come and
go between full-suite runs — ContactForm.test.tsx, LeadDetailModal.test.tsx and
SubmitReview.test.tsx. All three were run in isolation this iteration and passed
5/5, 3/3 and 7/7. They share a shape: async edge-function calls under fake
timers, timing out only when the suite is loaded. Whoever picks this up should
look at the shared waitFor timeout rather than at the individual specs.

### US-151 — stop auth and legal pages absorbing impressions — 2026-09-08 — PASSES

The story's premise checked out exactly. None of the seven auth pages set any
meta at all — no SEOHead, no Helmet, nothing — so every one of them inherited
index.html's marketing title and competed with the pages that sell the product.
/auth/login took 114 impressions and /auth/register 42.

robots.txt's `Disallow: /auth/` is removed, and that is the load-bearing change.
Disallow stops the crawl, not the indexing: Google had indexed /auth/login from
links alone and was forbidden from fetching the document that would have told it
not to. Adding a noindex while the Disallow stood would have changed nothing.
/api/ and /dashboard/ stay disallowed. The reasoning is written into robots.txt
so nobody restores it as an obvious tidy-up.

Six auth routes are now prerendered carrying <meta name="robots"
content="noindex, follow"> in the served HTML, and all six are excluded from
sitemap.xml via the `sitemap: false` flag US-149 added. Verified in the built
files: six auth pages noindex, and /, /pricing, /vs/linktree and /terms all
still "index, follow". Sitemap is 44 URLs with zero /auth/ entries.

Done at the route rather than in the pages. src/components/auth/AuthRouteSEO.tsx
wraps each auth element in App.tsx with a per-route title and description, so a
new auth route picks it up by construction and the seven components stay
untouched. Each title is distinct because `npm run verify:seo` fails on two
pages sharing one.

public/_headers additionally sends `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, follow` for /auth/*.
Belt and braces, and it is the only thing that covers an auth URL which is never
prerendered — which turned out to matter.

/auth/callback is deliberately NOT prerendered, and the gate is what found it.
Its whole job is to consume an OAuth code and redirect; with no code it lands on
/auth/login, so the snapshot written to dist/auth/callback/index.html was the
login page — confirmed by both files carrying the same title and the same
password field. verify:seo reported "/auth/login shares its <title> with
/auth/callback" and refused. Prerendering a redirect endpoint snapshots wherever
it redirected to. The X-Robots-Tag covers it instead. /auth/sso/callback renders
a real state rather than redirecting, so it keeps its file.

Two checks needed the same exemption, because a page carrying noindex has no use
for a canonical: scripts/lib/seo-audit.mjs already had it from US-150, and
scripts/prerender.mts now does too — it was failing all seven auth routes on a
missing canonical alone.

Legal pages: unchanged in indexability, already at sitemap priority 0.3 from
US-149. For internal-link prominence, PublicFooter linked /privacy, /terms and
/dmca three times each on every page of the site — a Legal column, a prose
paragraph in the legal notice, and a bottom-bar nav duplicating the column. The
bottom-bar set is removed. Every legal page is still linked at least once and
still one click away; they just stop taking three sitewide internal links each
while holding 207 of 1,481 impressions and converting none.

Verification: build exits 0 (50 routes rendered, 44 in the sitemap, 6
deliberately excluded), verify:seo passes on all 50, tsc --noEmit clean, eslint
clean on the four changed files, impeccable clean on the new component.

On the test suite, and this is worth stating precisely because the raw number
looks alarming: three consecutive full runs gave 13, 7 and 5 failures, with
durations of 91s, 71s and 54s. Same 645 tests each time. Failures track run
duration, not code. Every suspect passes in isolation — Register 3/3, Login 4/4,
SubmitReview 5/5, ContactForm 3/3, LeadDetailModal 7/7. The stable floor remains
the four that pre-date this branch (repo-hygiene x2 from 908a2c10's loose root
files, analytics, analyticsEvents). The jsdom component specs time out under
machine load; the first run followed a full production build on the same
machine. Someone should raise the shared waitFor timeout or cap the worker pool
— it is now producing enough noise to hide a real regression, which is the
actual risk here.

### US-152 — retarget the homepage at the query it can serve — 2026-09-08 — PASSES

  title  "Real Estate Agent Bio Page Builder | Turn Instagram Followers into Leads – AgentBio"
      -> "Link in Bio for Real Estate Agents | AgentBio"
  H1     "Real Estate Agent Bio Page Builder"
      -> "Link in Bio for Real Estate Agents"

The old title was 84 characters and Google truncated it mid-phrase — the SERP
showed "Real Estate Agent Bio Page Builder | Turn Instagram Follo...", so the
half describing the product never appeared. The new one is 45.

src/config/homepage-seo.ts is now the single source for title, description,
keywords, H1, H1 highlight and subtitle, with the Search Console numbers that
justify each written next to it. Landing.tsx renders it, and a `homepage-seo`
transformIndexHtml plugin in vite.config.ts writes the same strings into
index.html at build time — verified: dist/index.html carries the new title in
<title>, og:title and twitter:title, and the new description in description,
og:description and twitter:description, while the source index.html is only the
pre-transform input. The literals in index.html were updated to match anyway,
with a comment saying the file is rewritten at build time and that editing them
there alone is silently overwritten. og:image still resolves — dist/Cover.png,
591 KB — and twitter:card is still summary_large_image.

Two real defects found in the hero while doing it, neither in the story:

1. HeroSection splits the headline on its LAST TWO WORDS to decide what gets the
   highlight treatment. That is fine for "Real Estate Agent Bio | Page Builder"
   and silently mangles anything else: "Link in Bio for Real Estate Agents"
   would have rendered as "Link in Bio for Real" / "Estate Agents". Added an
   optional `titleHighlight` prop that says explicitly where the split belongs,
   falling back to the old positional behaviour so the five /features/* callers
   are untouched. Verified in the built HTML: the H1 renders as "Link in Bio
   for" / "Real Estate Agents".

2. HeroSectionLazy's HeroFallback — the lightweight hero shown while the 900 KB
   GSAP/Three chunk loads — HARDCODED "Real Estate Agent" / "Bio Page Builder",
   the subtitle and the description, and ignored every text prop passed to it.
   So on a slow connection the first paint contradicted the page's own <title>,
   the H1 that eventually replaced it, and the headline each of the five
   /features/* pages passes in. It now renders its props.

EXPECT IMPRESSIONS TO FALL, and that is the change working rather than failing.
The ~180 impressions from the "real estate agent bio" cluster (82 at position
88.6 for the head term alone) produced one click in sixteen months. US-155 is
what serves that intent properly; this story stops the homepage chasing it.
Baseline to measure against: 33 clicks / 1,481 impressions / position 18.4 over
the 16 months to 2026-09-08.

Verification: build exits 0 (50 routes), verify:seo passes all 50, tsc --noEmit
clean, eslint 0 errors (3 pre-existing unescaped-entity warnings).

One thing deliberately NOT changed: `npx impeccable detect` flags gradient text
on the hero H1 (bg-clip-text + bg-gradient), which CLAUDE.md's craft floor
refuses by name. It is pre-existing — the gradient span was already there and
this story only replaced the strings inside it — and removing it changes the
visual treatment of the homepage hero and five feature pages. That is a design
decision for Dj, not a side effect of an SEO retarget. Flagged, not touched.

Test suite, same story as US-151 and worth restating because the raw number
moves every run: 10 failures at 74s this time, 645 tests as always. The flaky
set now rotates through routes.test.ts and Settings.test.tsx as well.
routes.test.ts was the one worth taking seriously, since App.tsx changed in
US-151 — it passes 3/3 in isolation, as do Settings 6/6 and Register 3/3. Still
the same four stable pre-existing failures underneath.

### US-153 — gate the city pages behind noindex — 2026-09-08 — PASSES

All 26 /for/{city} pages now render with `noindex, follow` and are out of
sitemap.xml. The sitemap drops from 44 URLs to 21. Nothing is deleted: the
pages, the template and the data all stay, and they remain crawlable — which is
what lets Google read the directive at all.

The story's description checked out. One 715-line template, and the only things
that differ between any two pages are the city name, four numbers, one sentence
of marketDescription and a neighbourhood list. The title and description are
string substitution on the city name alone:
  "AgentBio for {city} Real Estate Agents | Instagram Bio & Lead Generation"
Swap Miami for Austin and you have the other page. 26 of those entering the
index at once, on a domain averaging position 18-20 for everything it has, is
the doorway-page shape — and this is a risk US-147 created rather than found.
While nothing prerendered they took zero impressions in 16 months and cost
nothing.

Mechanism: `indexable?: boolean` on LocationData, absent meaning no.
LocationTemplate's robots meta was hardcoded `index, follow, ...` and is now
conditional on it; locationRoutes() in prerender-routes.ts sets `sitemap: false`
unless the flag is set. Flipping one flag is the whole operation.

Verified in both directions, not just the safe one. With no flags set: Miami,
Austin and Denver all emit `noindex, follow` and none is in the sitemap, 0
/for/ URLs total. Then `indexable: true` was set on Miami temporarily and the
site rebuilt: Miami emitted `index, follow, max-image-preview:large,
max-snippet:-1` and appeared in sitemap.xml, while Austin stayed noindex and
absent. The temporary flag was then reverted — `grep -n indexable
src/data/locations.ts` returns only the interface field and the doc comment, no
data entry.

docs/seo/CITY_PAGES.md records the four things a page must have before the flag
goes on, and src/data/locations.ts's header points at it. The load-bearing test
in that doc is rule 2: if a sentence still reads correctly after swapping the
city name for a different city, it is not local content. That is what catches
most of it.

ZERO cities are switched on, and that is a deliberate reading of the criterion
rather than an omission. US-153 allowed up to two as worked examples "only if
they are given substantive unique content in this story". Substantive content
about the Miami or Austin housing market means verifiable claims with a source,
and inventing plausible-looking market data is exactly what the doc's first rule
exists to prevent — a fabricated median price does more damage than a noindexed
page does. The mechanism is built and proven; the first real city page is a
content task for somebody who knows that market. Written up as such in
CITY_PAGES.md rather than left implied.

Also noticed, not acted on: LocationTemplate emits
`<meta name="perplexity-verification" content="agentbio-verified" />`. There is
no such verification mechanism. Harmless, but it is cargo cult and someone
should delete it — flagging for US-124 rather than widening this story.

Verification: build exits 0 (50 routes rendered, 21 in the sitemap), verify:seo
passes all 50, tsc --noEmit clean, eslint 0 errors (5 pre-existing warnings).
Full suite 638 passed / 7 failed at 53s — the cleanest run of the batch so far —
and running the three failing files in isolation gives exactly the four stable
pre-existing failures (repo-hygiene x2, analytics, analyticsEvents), so the
other three were load flakes in those same files.

### US-154 — consolidate the blog — 2026-09-08 — BLOCKED, passes stays false

Not done, and deliberately not faked. The plan and the safety mechanism are
built; the content work needs production access this machine does not have.

What the data says, re-derived from the Search Console export rather than taken
from the story: 27 blog posts took impressions in the 16 months to 2026-09-08,
and between them 8 clicks and 605 impressions. Six of those clicks belong to
how-real-estate-agents-use-link-in-bio-to-generate-more-leads-in-2024 (162
impressions, position 11.09). The other 26 posts earned TWO clicks in sixteen
months. The story said 25 posts and 2 clicks; it is 26 and 2, and the extra post
does not change anything.

docs/seo/BLOG_CONSOLIDATION.md holds the full map, written before anything was
touched as the story requires: one kept pillar plus four proposed guides, with
all 26 retired slugs assigned to a survivor, each 301 pointing directly at its
final destination. Clusters are: the pillar absorbs the eight "what is a link in
bio / how do agents get leads" permutations; guide 1 takes the seven "what to
put on the page" posts; guide 2 the five listings/tours/selling ones; guide 3
the three rental and leasing ones, which are a genuinely different audience;
guide 4 the three portfolio/resume ones. 26 retired plus 1 kept accounts for all
27.

The pillar keeps its slug. Its "2024" framing gets refreshed in the copy, but
renaming the one URL on this site with earned position, for tidiness, would
throw away 18% of the site's clicks.

WHY IT IS BLOCKED. Merging 27 posts requires reading 27 posts. Their bodies
exist only in the production `articles` table — confirmed by grep: no seed
migration, no fixture, no copy anywhere in the repository; the only place those
slugs appear at all is prd.json. Writing four "consolidated" guides without
reading what they replace would mean inventing 27 posts' worth of content and
calling it a merge, which is the failure the plan exists to prevent rather than
a shortcut through it. Unpublishing the retired rows likewise needs a database
write.

And shipping the redirects early would be actively worse than doing nothing: 26
URLs that currently return 200 would 301 into guides that do not exist. So no
redirect was added. The order in the doc — write the guides, publish them, then
redirect, then unpublish, then rebuild — is not bureaucracy; reversing steps 1
and 2 breaks 26 live URLs.

WHAT WAS BUILT AND PROVEN. The step that makes executing the rest safe.
verifyServedLayout() in scripts/prerender.mts now rejects two things in
public/_redirects, and both were tested against the real build rather than
asserted:
  - a 301 whose target is not a page this build produced. Injected
    `/blog/some-retired-slug /blog/a-guide-nobody-wrote 301`; the build failed
    with "a live URL would 301 into a 404".
  - a 301 into another 301. Injected a two-hop chain; the build failed with
    "which is itself redirected — point it at the final destination instead".
  - and a legitimate `/blog/old-a /pricing 301` passes, so the check is not
    simply refusing everything.
External (http/https) targets and splat/placeholder rules are skipped rather
than guessed at.

So when somebody executes the plan, a mistake in the redirect map fails the
build instead of reaching Google. That is criteria 4 and 5 of the story
satisfied and demonstrated; criteria 1, 2, 6, 7 need the database.

Two unrelated dead internal links found while checking criterion 8, both in
src/lib/geo.ts: targetUrl '/blog/instagram-marketing-for-real-estate' (no such
post appears in 16 months of Search Console data) and '/compare' (no such route
— the comparison pages are at /vs/*). Nothing in src/ links to any of the 26
slugs being retired, so criterion 8 has nothing to do for this consolidation.
The geo.ts links belong to US-124 or US-156.

TO FINISH THIS STORY, someone with database access needs to:
  1. Reconcile the map against `select slug from articles where status =
     'published'` — Search Console only lists pages with at least one
     impression, so a post that took none in 16 months is not in the map.
  2. Write the four guides from the bodies of the posts they absorb, and expand
     the pillar. Publish them.
  3. Add the 301s to public/_redirects. The build will check them.
  4. `update articles set status = 'draft'` on the 26 retired rows. Do not
     delete: the content is the only copy.
  5. Rebuild. Retired slugs leave sitemap.xml on their own because it is
     generated from what rendered (US-149).

### US-155 — free agent bio generator — 2026-09-08 — PASSES

/tools/real-estate-agent-bio-generator ships, prerendered, in the sitemap, with
five worked examples as crawlable text. This is the page that serves the cluster
US-152 stopped the homepage chasing: "real estate agent bio" 82 impressions at
position 88.6, "professional real estate agent bio examples" at 7.5, plus the
new-agent, luxury and realtor-instagram variants — roughly 180 impressions over
16 months and one click, because there was no page for them.

Deterministic templates, no model call. src/lib/agent-bio-generator/ follows the
shape of the existing src/lib/instagram-bio-analyzer/bio-generator.ts — template
objects, a structure function per output shape, plain string assembly. No API
key, no edge function, nothing leaves the browser, and it works on first paint.
The two libraries stay separate on purpose: the existing one SCORES an existing
150-character Instagram bio; this one WRITES the professional bio an agent needs
for a brokerage page or MLS profile, which is what the queries are asking for.

Three outputs per run: a third-person professional paragraph, a first-person
short version, and one at 150 characters or fewer for the Instagram field. Five
niches, as the query data dictates: new agent, luxury, rentals/leasing, team,
general — each with its own focus line and closing line.

The worked examples are generated by the generator at module load rather than
written by hand, so what a crawler indexes cannot drift from what the tool
returns. Verified in the built HTML: all five example agents' names and their
bodies are present in dist/tools/real-estate-agent-bio-generator/index.html. No
example claims an award, a ranking or a sales figure — a bio-examples page is
precisely where an invented credential gets copied verbatim by a real agent, so
the illustrative details are limited to things that cannot be a false claim, and
the page says they are illustrative.

Three phrasing bugs were caught by actually reading the output rather than
trusting it: a 12-year agent rendered as "has spent more than 10 years"; a
leasing agent rendered as "I have been selling"; and the brokerage clause read
"Cascade & Co. is where Sam is licensed, serving Boise". All three fixed.

Functionally verified in a real browser, not just built: filled the form, chose
"New agent" and "Direct", submitted, and got the correct new-agent framing back
("is a newly licensed agent in Columbus…" rather than the 4-years text the
number field held), a 66/150 Instagram counter, and a working CTA to
/auth/register. No page errors. The copy button falls back silently when the
clipboard is denied, which is what headless does — the text stays selectable.

Analytics uses the existing gtag access pattern from src/lib/web-vitals.ts and
no-ops when GA is absent. Three events: bio_generated (with niche and tone),
bio_copied (with format), bio_cta_clicked. Deliberately NOT a new Supabase table
— the existing tool writes to instagram_bio_analytics, and adding a table here
would mean a migration and RLS policy this machine cannot verify against a real
database.

Craft floor: `npx impeccable detect` is clean on the new page, and it is
discriminating rather than broken — the same command still reports the hero's
gradient text. No gradients anywhere on the page, single elevation (border, no
shadow), rounded-2xl, body measure capped at 68-70ch, 44px minimum touch
targets, real fieldsets with legends and aria-pressed on the toggles.

Verification: build exits 0 (51 routes now), verify:seo passes all 51, tsc
--noEmit clean, eslint 0 problems on the new files. Full suite 641 passed / 4
failed at 46s — exactly the four stable pre-existing failures and the cleanest
run of the batch. routes.test.ts passes, which matters because a route was added.

Note for whoever measures this: the point is not traffic to the tool, it is
whether the tool feeds the funnel. bio_cta_clicked over bio_generated is the
number to watch. If people generate bios and never click through, the page is
serving an intent that does not convert and should be judged on that.

### US-156 — comparison pages — 2026-09-08 — PASSES

The story framed this as "make /vs/linktree substantive". What the pages
actually needed first was to stop asserting things that are not true.

FIVE FABRICATED TESTIMONIALS WERE LIVE ON THESE PAGES. Two on /vs/linktree
("Sarah M., Luxury Agent, Austin TX" claiming a jump from 1-2 leads a month to
8-10 qualified inquiries; "Mike R., Team Leader, Miami FL") and three on
/vs/beacons ("Marcus T.", "Jessica R.", "David K.", carrying the metrics "18
leads/month from Instagram", "3x more bio link clicks" and "$2.4M closed from
Instagram"). All hardcoded JSX, none from the `testimonials` table that the rest
of the product reads through useTestimonials — so nothing records who said them,
whether they said them, or whether they consented. A named endorsement with an
unverifiable revenue figure is exactly what the FTC endorsement guides cover.
Removed, with a comment at each site explaining what was there and why it went,
and how to reinstate them properly if these are real agents who agreed.

THREE PRICING CLAIMS WERE WRONG ABOUT OUR OWN PRODUCT.
  - /vs/linktree said "$39" in the comparison table and "$49/month" in the prose
    on the same page. $39 is not one of our plans; pricing-plans.ts has 0, 29,
    49, 99, 299.
  - /vs/later said "$19" in the table and "$29/mo" lower down. $19 is not a plan
    either, and a "$54/month total" figure was built on top of it.
Both now derive from PRICING_PLANS rather than being typed in.

COMPETITOR PRICES ARE GONE, AND THAT IS THE RIGHT ANSWER, not a shortfall. The
pages asserted "$24 (Pro)" for Linktree, "$10/month" for Beacons and "$25-$80"
for Later, all unsourced. Checking linktr.ee/s/pricing on 2026-09-08 returned
the tier names but no figures: Linktree shows pricing in local currency, it
varies by region, and their own page warns that tiers and boundaries change
frequently. A single USD number on our site would be wrong for most readers on
most days, and being wrong about a competitor's price is both a credibility and
a legal problem. The pages now compare tiers and capabilities, link to the
vendor so a reader can check in one click, and say plainly that we do not quote
their prices and why.

src/config/competitors.ts is the single source: tier names, what each product is
genuinely built for, and — the part that makes a comparison page credible —
`betterWhen`, an honest list of when to pick them over us. COMPETITORS_VERIFIED_ON
is dated 2026-09-08 and rendered on /vs/linktree, so a stale date is visible to
the reader rather than only to us. Update the date in the same commit as the
facts.

Also removed: "Why 2,000+ Agents Switched from Linktree to AgentBio" — an
unverifiable customer count in the hero subtitle.

THE PAGES WERE ORPHANED, which is a large part of why all three took zero
impressions in 16 months even before the prerender problem. Nothing on the site
linked to them — not the header, not the footer, not /pricing. Added a "Compare
to Linktree" link to the footer's Product column (sitewide) and a line at the
end of the pricing FAQ pointing at all three, worded to include that they say
where the competitor is the better choice. Someone on the pricing page comparing
us to something else is precisely the audience.

Fixed src/lib/geo.ts's targetUrl '/compare', which has never been a route, to
'/vs/linktree'. The other dead link there,
'/blog/instagram-marketing-for-real-estate', is left for US-124 — it belongs to
the blog, not to this story.

Craft floor: `npx impeccable detect` is now clean on all three pages. It flagged
gradient text in two places — the AgentBio column header in /vs/beacons and the
H1 on /vs/later — and unlike the hero (which restyles six pages and is Dj's
call), these are a single table header and a single heading inside pages this
story explicitly covers, so they were fixed rather than deferred. Emphasis now
comes from weight and the brand colour. All three comparison tables already had
overflow-x-auto wrappers, so the mobile criterion needed nothing.

Verification: build exits 0 (51 routes), verify:seo passes all 51, tsc --noEmit
clean, eslint 0 errors (46 pre-existing warnings). All three /vs/ pages are in
the sitemap; the footer link appears on every prerendered page. Confirmed in the
built HTML that "Marcus T.", "Jessica R.", "$2.4M" and "2,000+ Agents" no longer
appear anywhere in dist/.

Full suite 634 passed / 11 failed at 90s, which is the load-flaky pattern
(failures track duration). routes.test.ts was worth checking because Pricing.tsx
changed: 3/3 in isolation, LeadDetailModal 7/7, and the three stable files give
exactly the four known pre-existing failures.

>>> SITE-WIDE FINDING, BEYOND THIS STORY'S SCOPE, FOR DJ TO DECIDE ON <<<
The fabricated testimonials are not confined to the comparison pages. Still live
elsewhere, hardcoded, none from the testimonials table:
  src/pages/tools/ListingDescriptionGenerator.tsx:250  "Sarah M., Beverly Hills"
  src/pages/tools/ListingDescriptionGenerator.tsx:257  "Mike T., Austin"
  src/pages/tools/ListingDescriptionGenerator.tsx:264  "Jennifer L., Denver"
